# Benin

Wealth gradients in fertility and mortality: the values for an OG-Core calibration, followed by the estimates they are based on. Terms are defined in the [glossary](../glossary.md).

## Values for OG-Core

| OG-Core input | Wealth gradient | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `fert_gradient` | −0.59, by age as below | DHS 2017, TFR, plus [age offsets](../methods/fertility-by-age.md) |
| `infmort_gradient` | −0.52 | DHS 2017, infant mortality rate |
| `mort_gradient` | −0.57 | census 2013, 45q15 |
| `imm_pctiles` | not provided | — |

Values are [wealth gradients](../glossary.md#wealth-gradient). Before they are passed to OG-Core, each is divided by 100 × (1 − p), where p is OG-Core's rate at that age ([details](../methods/ogcore-units.md)).

**Fertility gradient by age of mother** (`fert_gradient`; ages below 15 use the 15–19 value, ages 50 and above the 45–49 value):

| 15–19 | 20–24 | 25–29 | 30–34 | 35–39 | 40–44 | 45–49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.37 | −0.69 | −0.38 | −0.26 | −0.50 | −0.98 | −1.57 |

Source: IPUMS International (Ruggles et al., doi:10.18128/D020.V7.7); original data: Institut National de la Statistique et de l'Analyse Economique, Benin.

## Notes

- The 2013 census records deaths since 1 January 2012, a reference period of about 16 months. Recorded deaths are about 35 percent of the expected national total; the shortfall is similar across wealth groups and does not affect the gradient, but rate levels are not meaningful.
